A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same RoMAE research work. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and matchable despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original position-reconstruction experiments, classification and interpolation benchmarks, and qualitative examples, including the audio evaluation in Appendix A.4.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical evaluations, revises several benchmark results, and adds runtime and frequency-retention experiments.

M1.justification: The continuous axial p-RoPE, patchification, optional [CLS] token, asymmetric encoder/decoder and prediction heads are retained. Expanded RMSNorm and patch-loss normalization descriptions document existing components without establishing an algorithmic change. Additional model-size evaluations use configurations already defined in v1.

E1.justification: Appendix B.4 adds controlled interpolation of single- and double-frequency sinusoidal signals, plus reported square-wave and cycloid checks. Existing benchmark coverage is retained. Moving audio into the main text and changing ELAsTiCC2 terminology do not establish additional datasets.

E2.justification: The new runtime comparison in Table 9 evaluates continuous RoPE against absolute sinusoidal embeddings and quantized RoPE. Prediction-benchmark comparator sets remain unchanged, including SSAST, ATAT, and the UEA, Pendulum and interpolation baselines; the relocated audio comparison is not a new baseline addition.

E3.justification: Reported settings change substantially: Tiny ImageNet fine-tuning switches from SGD to AdamW with unified hyperparameters and FP32; audio pretraining changes from 50–100 to 150 epochs; ELAsTiCC changes batches and precision and adds a size control. UEA prose changes from 800 to 400 epochs, matching its retained appendix table. New runtime and frequency experiments also introduce evaluation protocols.

E4.justification: v2 adds positional-encoding runtime comparisons, extensive frequency-retention analyses with time-domain and Fourier-domain errors, and nonsinusoidal checks (Appendices B.2 and B.4). The added ELAsTiCC tiny-shallow result controls model capacity relative to ATAT. These substantially expand efficiency, sensitivity and capacity analyses beyond v1.

E5.justification: Tiny ImageNet Table 2 newly reports standard deviations, although its run count is unspecified. The new frequency analysis reports variability across 200 series per frequency. Existing seed and repeated-evaluation descriptions are retained; the PDFs do not establish an increase in runs for retained experiments.

E6.justification: Tiny ImageNet no-[CLS] F-score changes from 0.3471 to 0.500; ELAsTiCC's 0.6770 is replaced by 0.7106 and 0.8029 for two sizes. ESC-50 accuracies change from 81.0/83.4 to 83.2/84.7 for Librispeech/AudioSet-20k pretraining. These accompany revised settings. PhysioNet changes from 0.570 ± 0.014 to 0.467 ± 0.021 in the table, while the discussion retains the old value. Runtime/frequency results are added; Tiny ImageNet precision and recall entries are removed.

T1.justification: Equation (3) expands the RMS-only definition into the normalized RMSNorm output, including learned gains and a numerical-stability epsilon. The RoPE propositions, corollaries, [CLS] definition and constructive absolute-position proof retain their mathematical substance after relocation.

C1.justification: Introduction contribution 1 narrows its assertion from evidence that RoPE information does not decay with distance to insights about embedding varying positional scales. The abstract explicitly mentions interpolation, already evaluated in v1. The central versatility, performance and learned-token claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds sampling and spectral explanations for frequency-dependent errors, caching explanations for runtime overhead, and a recommendation to rescale positions. Tiny ImageNet discussion offers translation invariance or mean pooling as explanations, and ELAsTiCC discussion acknowledges model size. Existing extrapolation and sequence-length limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 announces a public Python package with an access link, supplies audio fine-tuning hyperparameters, adds parameter counts, and documents patch-loss normalization and timing hardware. Numerous implementation disclosures are revised, including ELAsTiCC hardware from H100 to A100. These substantially expand reproducibility information without independently establishing which experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: Appendix B.4 adds Rahaman et al. and Xu et al. on spectral bias, connecting the new analysis to that literature. The main MAE, RoPE and irregular-time-series positioning remains. Reference renumbering, publication metadata updates and duplicate-reference consolidation do not represent additional changes in research coverage.

P1.justification: Audio moves from Appendix A.4 into Section 5.3; the mixed appendix is reorganized into separate model-details and analysis appendices; experimental subsections are reordered; acknowledgments move after the conclusion. Together with rewritten experimental passages, this constitutes substantial structural reorganization despite largely retained method prose.

P2.justification: v2 adds three frequency-analysis figures and a runtime table, revises the architecture and light-curve illustrations, restructures Tiny ImageNet and ELAsTiCC result tables, and consolidates training-parameter tables. Several tables also receive side-by-side layouts. These are substantial display changes beyond numerical updates and renumbering.

improvement.justification: The runtime and frequency analyses, ELAsTiCC capacity control, Tiny ImageNet uncertainty reporting, and expanded reproducibility information strengthen the evidence and make the paper easier to assess. The improvement is limited by unresolved consistency problems: v2 Table 7 reports PhysioNet MSE of 0.467 ± 0.021, while Section 6 retains 0.570 ± 0.014 and its earlier interpretation. Higher scores alone do not establish the quality gain.
